stem: Chlorine is a very reactive element.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Chlorine reacts with silicon to form silicon(IV) chloride.
Describe the appearance of silicon(IV) chloride at room temperature and pressure. State its structure and bonding.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: State the reagent and conditions required for the formation of sodium chlorate(V) from $\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the reaction in (c)(i) is described as a disproportionation reaction. Your answer should refer to relevant species and their oxidation numbers.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: Chlorine reacts with methane in a series of reactions to produce chloroalkanes.
parts.text: State the conditions required for chlorine to react with methane.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
One of the products of the reaction is $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ which reacts further to produce $\text{CHCl}_3$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
$\text{CHCl}_3$ and $\text{HF}$ are used to form $\text{CHClF}_2$ in a substitution reaction.

Construct an equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:

There is only one naturally occurring isotope of fluorine, $^{19}\text{F}$.
